---
title: "Sloan Annotated"
---

Annotated rebuilds of MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference research papers. Each paper becomes a page you can read, run, and push back on in the browser. The stack is a Quarto website: Python in the page through Pyodide, and charts in Plotly or D3. No account, no kernel.

The work is inspired by annotated implementations, and aimed at learning. A page is finished when a reader can see the question, the data, the method, the paper's figure next to ours, and where the rebuild held or broke.

## Open the template

The first rebuild is [penalty-kick location](papers/penalty-kick-location/index.qmd). The [page template](papers/_template/index.qmd) is the working example of every section and widget. Copy it for each paper. Do not invent a second layout.

The [paper list](papers/index.qmd) names the first five rebuilds in build order. Each one already has a directory under `papers/`. The page is marked coming soon until `index.qmd` is there. Allowed sources are StatsBomb open data, NFL Big Data Bowl releases, nflverse, Baseball Savant, the penalty-kick authors' repository, OptimalDarts, Metrica Sports sample tracking data, and Retrosheet. The license and the credit line for each source are in `PLAN.md`. A page that is not on the paper's own data says so, in a callout titled "Rebuilt on substitute data."

## How a paper gets on the site

A scout writes `papers/<name>/BRIEF.md`. A builder turns that brief into code and one interactive page, in one pull request. A checker reads the page against the paper. Jordan approves every merge. Coding agents do not merge.

The repository README has the preview command and the directory map. `PLAN.md` is the longer spec.
